brief.title: Intermittent Fasting and Blood Pressure: Recent PubMed Evidence
brief.summary: Recent PubMed studies show early time‑restricted feeding lowers blood pressure in men with prediabetes, even without weight loss, and combined with energy restriction reduces diastolic pressure more than late eating or restriction alone; a 3‑month RCT supports these findings.

points.text: Early time‑restricted feeding lowers blood pressure in prediabetic men without weight loss.
Early time‑restricted eating with energy restriction cuts diastolic pressure more than late eating or restriction alone.
The findings come from a 3‑month randomized clinical trial.

gaps: Long‑term blood pressure effects beyond 3 months not reported.
Other intermittent fasting schedules (e.g., alternate‑day fasting) not examined.
Study population limited to men with prediabetes; women and older adults not included.
No data on systolic blood pressure changes.
